key_insight: Q-DICE provides a hardware-aware compiler and emulator that lets researchers benchmark distributed quantum circuits with realistic interconnect constraints and noise.
engineering_relevance: It helps co-design distributed quantum hardware and algorithms by reproducing topology limits, link noise, and mapping behavior before physical systems are widely available.
method: Builds distributed QPU backends via QPU slicing and stitching
Models nonlocal link noise with Kraus operators and stochastic error channels
Uses boundary-aware transpilation to enforce distributed topology constraints
evidence_signal: The framework was validated on multiple experimentally demonstrated circuits, including distributed Grover's search, with up to 4% worst-case fidelity deviation from hardware results.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well the chosen noise model and topology assumptions match the target distributed hardware.
paper_title: Q-DICE: Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler and Emulator
